title: MCA ACH Debits: Payment Adjustments, Bank Disputes, and Contract Risks
excerpt: What to check when MCA withdrawals strain cash flow: reconciliation terms, unauthorized debits, business-account deadlines, and the risks of stopping payments.
author: Business Debt Insider
contentMd:
When MCA withdrawals leave too little cash for payroll or suppliers, separate two questions: is the debit authorized and correctly calculated, and can the business afford the agreed payment? The response to an incorrect withdrawal can differ from the response to an unaffordable but authorized one.

**Editorial correction — October 11, 2026:** This guide replaces unsupported response percentages and timelines, a generic ACH-revocation template, and advice to reroute operating funds. It does not promise that a reconciliation request pauses withdrawals or prevents default.

## First identify the agreement and the withdrawal

Collect the signed financing agreement, ACH authorization, amendments, transaction dates, amounts, bank statements, and correspondence. Match the originator shown by the bank with the company servicing the agreement; a trade name alone may not identify the legal counterparty.

Then identify the issue:

| Situation | Information to gather | Initial contact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue declined and the payment no longer fits | Revenue records and the agreement's adjustment provisions | Servicer or funder |
| Withdrawal differs from the written authorization | Authorization, transaction details, and relevant correspondence | Bank's business ACH team and servicer |
| Debits continue after a documented payoff | Payoff confirmation and account history | Bank and servicer |
| Default notice, lawsuit, or account restraint | Complete notice, service date, court papers, and contract | A lawyer licensed for the relevant matter |

Do not wait for a general consultation to report a suspected unauthorized transaction to your bank. Ask the bank what documentation and deadlines apply to the specific account and entry.

## Payment adjustment and reconciliation

Read the actual provision before sending a request. A revenue-based financing agreement may distinguish a prospective payment adjustment from reconciliation of earlier collections. A business loan may have different modification terms or none of those mechanisms.

For example, [Forward Financing's published contract highlights](https://www.forwardfinancing.com/resources/forward-revenue-based-financing-contract-highlights/) describe revenue-based payment adjustments and reconciliation. That is evidence about that published product, not a promise about every funder or a loan bearing the same brand.

A request should identify the relevant clause, the period covered, the revenue figures used, and the supporting documents required by the agreement. Ask the servicer to confirm receipt, any missing information, the decision, and the payment amount and date that will apply if approved.

**Sending a request is not the same as obtaining a payment pause.** Keep written confirmation of any agreed change. If the response does not match the contract or the request is disputed, an independent lawyer can assess the clause and the available remedies.

## Business-account ACH disputes need prompt attention

Consumer and business accounts do not necessarily have the same protections or reporting windows. The [CFPB's Regulation E FAQs](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/compliance-resources/deposit-accounts-resources/electronic-fund-transfers/electronic-fund-transfers-faqs/) describe covered accounts as those established primarily for personal, family, or household purposes. Do not assume the consumer rules apply to your operating account.

[Nacha's explanation of unauthorized-debit return timing](https://www.nacha.org/rules/limitation-warranty-claims) describes a short network deadline for a bank returning an unauthorized debit to a non-consumer account: availability to the originating bank by the opening of the second banking day after settlement. This is a bank-to-bank return deadline, not a universal statement about every customer's contractual rights or all possible remedies. Your bank may need notice sooner to act within it.

Ask the bank which procedure fits the transaction, when it needs your instructions, whether supporting statements are required, and what can still be done if the ordinary return window has passed. Describe the facts accurately. The bank determines the appropriate processing and return code; this article does not tell you to label an authorized payment as unauthorized.

## A debit block does not resolve the financing agreement

A stop-payment instruction, debit filter, authorization dispute, and settlement agreement are different things. A banking action may affect movement of money without changing the obligations in the financing contract.

Before intentionally interrupting an authorized payment, obtain advice on default provisions, possible fees, security interests, guarantees, and any pending litigation. Do not assume a provider's enrollment agreement binds the funder or suspends its rights. BDI cannot promise that a bank block will prevent collections or litigation.

Do not move money or change collection accounts based on a generic online template. Account changes can affect contractual obligations, other creditors, and court orders. Any proposed change should be evaluated against the actual facts and documented advice.

## Questions to ask before agreeing to a workout

- Who will contact the servicer, and who is responsible for bank instructions?
- What written agreement changes the payment, and when does it take effect?
- Does the proposed change affect total payback or only timing?
- Which fees will the business pay in addition to creditor payments?
- What happens if a funder declines the proposal or files suit?
- Who holds any program funds, who can withdraw them, and what are the cancellation terms?

Keep an account-by-account record of the current payment authorization and any approved amendments. Use the [stack calculator](/tools/stack-calculator) to organize scheduled outflows; its estimated remaining payments are not a payoff quote.

## If you suspect deceptive or unauthorized collection

The [FTC has reported enforcement concerning unauthorized MCA withdrawals](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2020/08/small-businesses-targeted-unauthorized-withdrawals). That does not establish that a particular withdrawal in your account was unlawful. Preserve records, contact the bank promptly, and obtain advice about the facts. A complaint or negotiation does not replace responding to court papers by the required deadline.

For company-specific product and servicing sources, start with the [lender research directory](/lenders). For help organizing a review, [contact BDI](/contact). BDI is a financial consulting business, not a law firm; legal advice must come from independent, appropriately licensed counsel.
